definition: The central unit of content: a Markdown article with a title, slug, optional summary, and publication state. The aggregate root everything else hangs off of.

The only way posts are grouped: a topic or collection label (e.g. Development, Work Recap). A post carries zero or more tags and a tag spans many posts. Tags are created by typing them on a post; there are no categories and no series. Curated groupings are collections, built from tag rules.

A titled, described view over the posts, defined by tag rules. It stores no posts of its own: its page lists every published post that satisfies all of its rules, and a collection with no rules lists every post. Collections are listed on the home page.
A reader's response attached to a published post. May reply to another comment (threaded). Always moderated.
A post that has been saved but not published; private to the author.
A post visible to readers, with a publication timestamp.

A finished post that only the signed-in author can read. It keeps its slug, date and tags and appears to the author across the site with a Private badge, but to readers it does not exist: not on its page, not in any list, not in any count.

The date shown on a post and used to order public listings. Stamped automatically the first time a post is published; the author can change it afterwards in the editor. It is a label, not a schedule: a future date does not hide the post.

Automatic, periodic saving while writing (at most once a minute, only when something changed). Never changes publication state: it never publishes a draft nor unpublishes a post. Applies to drafts and published posts alike — a published post's autosaved edits go live immediately.

Deleting a post marks it deleted (deletedAt) and releases its slug rather than removing the row. The post and its comments are hidden from every surface but retained in the database, recoverable there.
A submitted comment awaiting the author's moderation; the default state of every new comment. Invisible to the public.
A comment the author has approved; visible to the public on its post.
A comment the author has marked as spam; hidden from the public.
One condition of a collection: the post must carry a given tag. A collection may have several; a post must satisfy all of them.
A collection's author-set position in the home page's collection list. New collections go last; the author reorders them by dragging in the admin.

The URL-safe identifier for a post, a tag, or a collection; unique within its type and may contain non-ASCII characters such as Hangul. A post's slug is service-managed: absent while the post is a draft, generated from the title when it is published, and de-duplicated with a numeric suffix (-2, -3…) on collision; it can change if the title changes.
Estimated minutes to read a post (~200 wpm, minimum 1), shown as N분 when available.
An optional short summary of a post, shown in list views.
A simple per-post view counter — the only analytic kept (see Out of Scope).
The single privileged user (Inho). Authenticates via the homelab SSO (Authentik OIDC). There is exactly one.
Any anonymous public visitor. No accounts, no login.
